"Ravens X2" has two of four top prizes left and is near the midpoint of its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Everything above about "Ravens X2" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
807.headline: How far along this game is

808.body:
About half of the tickets for "Ravens X10" have been sold. The game is in the middle of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

If you play "Ravens X10" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
808.headline: How much has sold

809.body:
"Gold Bar Bingo" has gone two weeks without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $50,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Today's free summary of "Gold Bar Bingo" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
809.headline: Top prizes are still left

810.body:
"In the Green" is down to four top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Everything above about "In the Green" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
810.headline: A top prize was just claimed

811.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Extreme Green" are sold. The top prize count has held, with four of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Everything here about "Extreme Green" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 8.
811.headline: No new top prize claims

812.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Loose Change®" are sold. The top prize count has held, with fifteen of 24 still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

If "Loose Change®" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
812.headline: Three weeks, no top prize claimed

813.body:
"The Price is Right™" has 374,393 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with eight left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
813.headline: What the prize table shows

814.body:
"High Voltage" is in the middle of its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Every line of High Voltage's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
814.headline: How much has sold

815.body:
One of $100,000 Crossword's top prizes was claimed last week. A player in Maryland won $100,000. The game started with nine top prizes and now has seven top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

The numbers for "$100,000 Crossword" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
815.headline: The top prize list got shorter

816.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Deluxe Crossword", about three-quarters are still unsold. The game is early in its run, with six of eight top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Today's free summary of "Deluxe Crossword" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
816.headline: How much has sold

817.body:
On "Hello Money!", one $50,000 top prize was claimed over a week ago. That leaves five of the original seven. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

If "Hello Money!" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
817.headline: Top prize count went down

818.body:
The prize money on "10X Cash" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over seven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $10,000. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Tomorrow's count on "10X Cash" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
818.headline: How the prize money is divided

819.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "30X Cash", about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

Everything here about "30X Cash" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 8.
819.headline: How prizes are split

820.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Cozy Cash", most are still unsold. The game is early in its run, with 33 of 35 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Every line of Cozy Cash's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.

Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "Holly-Day Cash" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
823.headline: How much has sold

824.body:
"Winter Multiplier" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $100,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold eight of the original nine. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "Winter Multiplier" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
